newsitem.title: USA: Dow falls as expiration volatility dominates.
newsitem.headline: Dow falls as expiration volatility dominates.

text.p: Stocks edged lower Friday as "double- witching" expirations whipped the market, distracting investors from the strength in bonds and favourable economic fundamentals.

"Today is all options-oriented and not an impressive performance at all following yesterday's sell-off," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "The market is reflecting the action in the derivatives pits more than anything else."
Stock index and individual stock options were to expire Friday, an occurrence known as double witching.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 4.23 points at 6,923.15. In the broader market, declining shares were even with those advancing on volume of about 278 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 10.33 points to 1,337.07.
The benchmark 30-year bond rose 8/32, reducing the yield to 6.63 percent from 6.65 percent Thursday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

The disaster of the day occured in shares of Scholastic Corp., down 25-1/4 at 36-1/4 in vigorous trading, a day after it warned of a third-quarter loss and a decline in fiscal year earnings. Downgrades from Merrill Lynch, Smith Barney, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and UBS Securities helped drag the stock to a 12-month low of 33-1/4.
The Dow Jones industrial average remained within a narrow range compared with recent sessions, but the average moved in volatile jumps.
"I think we are in a highly volatile atmosphere, expirations or no expirations," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"A situation like that can only exacerbate the effect of the options expirations. But if you stop and think about it, we've been in a pretty narrow range all day," he said.

High technology shares took a beating. Intel Corp. was down 2-5/8 at 147-1/4 and at the top of Nasdaq's most active list. Cascade Communications Corp. was down 2-5/8 at 26-1/4. Cisco Systems Inc. fell 2-3/8 to 60-5/8.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Semiconductor Index was down 6.33 points, or 2.23 percent, at 277.

"More high tech misery," Bleier said. "There are continuing concerns about future growth and the correctional rotation that has been going on in the sector. We are closer to a near-term bottom than top, but that doesn't mean that we are not in for more pain."

SoundView Financial Corp. said the personal computer industry's gross margins have peaked for the foreseeable future and that many PC makers are likely to follow Compaq Computer Corp. with price cuts in the second quarter.
Compaq was down 2-7/8 at 79-5/8. Dell Computer Corp. was down 7/8 at 71-5/8 and Gateway 2000 Inc. fell 1-3/8 to 60-5/8.
